title: Stoker's Epistolary Vampire: 1897 and the Fin de Siècle
welcome_lead: Enter Bram Stoker's 1897 novel and trace how the epistolary form, late-Victorian anxieties, and Gothic tradition combine to produce the modern vampire.
meta_desc: A-Level adventure on Stoker's Dracula (1897): epistolary form, fin de siècle anxieties, and Gothic tradition.
final_note: Dracula's victory over the Count is also the triumph of bourgeois documentation: typewriters, phonographs and shorthand defeat the ancient evil.

walkthroughs.body_html: Dracula was published by Archibald Constable in May 1897, the year of Victoria's Diamond Jubilee. Britain was at imperial zenith yet anxious: degeneration theory (Lombroso, Nordau), Irish nationalism, fears of immigrant 'aliens' from Eastern Europe, and the 1885 Criminal Law Amendment Act (under which Oscar Wilde was tried in 1895) all shape the novel's atmosphere. Stoker, an Anglo-Irish Protestant managing the Lyceum Theatre, channels these anxieties through Gothic form.

The novel comprises Jonathan Harker's journal (shorthand), Mina's typed diary, Dr Seward's phonograph entries, Lucy's letters, news cuttings, and ship's logs. Mina assembles them into a master document. Critics including Friedrich Kittler (Discourse Networks 1900) read the novel as a triumph of mediated, technologised information: the Count, an oral-feudal entity, is defeated by the bourgeois office.

Stephen Arata's 1990 essay 'The Occidental Tourist' coined 'reverse colonisation' to describe the Victorian fear that subject populations might return and contaminate the metropole. Dracula's purchase of London properties, his shipment of Transylvanian earth, and his predation on English women dramatise this anxiety. The novel both indulges and critiques imperial paranoia — Dracula's threat is ultimately neutralised by Anglo-American-Dutch cooperation.

mcqs.q: What are conventions of the Gothic genre?
options: Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
Settings of ruin and decay, supernatural or psychological terror, transgression of boundaries, the sublime, doubled or haunted protagonists, and atmospheric excess.
Gothic just means scary stories with vampires and ghosts.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
When the audience knows something a character does not, creating tension between the character's words/actions and the audience's understanding.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Dramatic irony is when something ironic happens in a play.
